answer: An identity is admitted only by posting a 500-token bond and a one-per-device credential, so each registry entry maps to a single vertex in the keyed attestation graph. A fake identity therefore locks 500 tokens for 30 epochs, all slashed on proven duplication. Splitting one device into many claimants raises marginal cost per copy, and any harbor of shared bonds forfeits the full pool once independent jurors trace one tainted echo.
